title: DIVA-GRPO: Enhancing Multimodal Reasoning through Difficulty-Adaptive Variant Advantage
claim: Prior methods use only a subset of samples or expand them without regard to difficulty; ours expands adaptively to keep a stable difficulty distribution.
layout: 3 panels split by dashed line, previous left, ours right, density plots
description: The figure is split by a vertical dashed line. The left half is headed 'Previous works' and holds two ellipse sketches, each with a red warning icon. Panel (a), selective sample utilization, shows a clipped slice of the origin problem space, with a hard-to-easy gradient arrow beneath. Panel (b), sample enhancement and expansion, shows a small origin ellipse inside a larger gray ellipse of problem variants. Purple dashed arrows run from a question Q to variants Q1, Q2 and Q3. The right half is headed 'Ours' and is panel (c), difficulty-adaptive problem expansion. It shows two ellipses with pink-to-blue difficulty gradients. Variants are sampled toward the under-represented difficulty end, and a green 'Train Steps' arrow links the two stages. At far right, two probability-density-versus-difficulty plots compare the expanded space (blue) with the origin space (orange). The expanded curve stays broad and centered. The eye goes first to the colorful ellipses.
caption: (a) Selective sample utilization relies on only a subset of data, leading to underuse. (b) Sample enhancement expands data without difficulty awareness, causing even severe advantage sparsity. (c) Our method adaptively expands the sample space by problem difficulty, ensuring a stable difficulty distribution.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) with group relative policy optimization (GRPO) has become a widely adopted approach for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). While GRPO enables long-chain reasoning without a critic, it often suffers from sparse rewards on difficult problems and advantage vanishing when group-level rewards are too consistent for overly easy or hard problems. Existing solutions (sample expansion, selective utilization, and indirect reward design) often fail to maintain enough variance in within-group reward distributions to yield clear optimization signals. To address this, we propose DIVA-GRPO, a difficulty-adaptive variant advantage method that adjusts variant difficulty distributions from a global perspective. DIVA-GRPO dynamically assesses problem difficulty, samples variants with appropriate difficulty levels, and calculates advantages across local and global groups using difficulty-weighted and normalized scaling. This alleviates reward sparsity and advantage vanishing while improving training stability. Extensive experiments on six reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DIVA-GRPO outperforms existing approaches in training efficiency and reasoning performance.
